questionText:
Consider contiguous allocation of physical memory to processes using variable partitioning scheme. Suppose there are 8 holes in the memory of sizes 20 KB, 4 KB, 25 KB, 18 KB, 7 KB, 9 KB, 15 KB, and 12 KB. Assume that no two holes are adjacent. Two processes P1 of size 16 KB and P2 of size 9 KB arrive in that order, and they are allocated memory using the best-fit technique. After allocating space to P1 and P2, the number of holes of size less than 8 KB is ____________. (answer in integer)

Note: 1K=$2^{10}$
explanation:
Step 1: Initial list of hole sizes
The initial sizes of the 8 holes are: 20 KB, 4 KB, 25 KB, 18 KB, 7 KB, 9 KB, 15 KB, and 12 KB.

Step 2: Allocation for Process P1 (16 KB) using Best-Fit
• The Best-Fit strategy selects the smallest hole that is large enough ($ \ge 16\text{ KB}$).
• Candidate holes $\ge 16\text{ KB}$: 20 KB, 25 KB, 18 KB.
• Smallest candidate hole is 18 KB.
• Allocation: P1 is placed in the 18 KB hole.
• Remaining size of this hole = $18\text{ KB} - 16\text{ KB} = 2\text{ KB}$.

Step 3: Allocation for Process P2 (9 KB) using Best-Fit
• Current hole sizes: 20 KB, 4 KB, 25 KB, 2 KB, 7 KB, 9 KB, 15 KB, 12 KB.
• Candidate holes $\ge 9\text{ KB}$: 20 KB, 25 KB, 9 KB, 15 KB, 12 KB.
• Smallest candidate hole is 9 KB.
• Allocation: P2 is placed in the 9 KB hole.
• Remaining size of this hole = $9\text{ KB} - 9\text{ KB} = 0\text{ KB}$ (hole is fully allocated).

Step 4: Count holes with size less than 8 KB
The final list of remaining holes is: 20 KB, 4 KB, 25 KB, 2 KB, 7 KB, 15 KB, 12 KB.
Holes of size less than 8 KB are:
1. 4 KB
2. 2 KB
3. 7 KB

Thus, the number of holes of size less than 8 KB is 3.
